headline: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B as AI megarounds pile up
what: AI drug-discovery company Isomorphic Labs raised a $5B Series C, reported on 18 Nov. The same day Genesis AI raised $500M at a $3.5B valuation for dexterous industrial robots.
why: Capital is concentrating in a few very large AI bets. For everyone else, the bar for a raise is proof of revenue, and competing for AI talent against $5B war chests gets harder.

tryThis.text: List the two or three AI-funded competitors in your space and what their latest round lets them spend on. Ask what you'd do with a tenth of it.

headline: Indian startup funding fell 90% in a week, to $25M
what: Indian startups raised just $25.2M between 9 and 13 Nov, down 90.1% from $255M the week before, per Inc42. October's VC total was $581M against $1.6B a year earlier, per YourStory Research.
why: Indian founders are raising in a drought while global AI rounds balloon. Expect slower hiring, longer runways, more down rounds, and more acqui-hire and partnership offers to land on your desk.

tryThis.text: If you partner with Indian startups, check which ones raised in the last 12 months. Plan for vendors that might cut scope or shut down.

real.label: Tracker data
real.reason: Weekly and monthly totals from two independent Indian trackers (Inc42, YourStory Research) that point the same way.

headline: Mastercard and Ant prove AI agents can pay, with limits
what: Mastercard and Ant International's Antom completed a live AI-agent purchase (a coffee, on the buyer's pre-verified intent) and a Singapore pilot where a business agent bought services within set spending limits.
why: Agentic payments are moving from demos to rails. Products that pay, lend or insure will need to answer: which agent is this, what was it allowed to do, and who's liable if it goes wrong.

tryThis.text: Take one payment flow in your product and write down what you'd need to let a customer's AI agent complete it safely: identity, limits, consent record, refunds.

real.label: Pilot completed
real.reason: Confirmed by both companies' announcement and multiple outlets; a controlled pilot, not a general rollout.

headline: Fintechs keep turning into banks: Qonto and OakNorth win licences
what: French business-banking fintech Qonto received a credit institution licence to expand lending and savings. UK lender OakNorth secured a US national bank charter after its Community Unity Bank deal was approved, per The Paypers (20 Nov).
why: A licence lets a fintech hold deposits and lend on its own balance sheet instead of renting a partner bank. In India, this is the bank-partner vs. own-licence trade-off every lending and insurance product faces.

tryThis.text: List which of your product's features depend on a partner's licence. For each, note what would change if the partner pulled out or the rules tightened.

real.label: Reported approvals
real.reason: Reported by trade press; we haven't seen the regulators' own notices, and OakNorth's approval had earlier been held up by the Fed.

headline: Two Millennium Prize claims in one day. Both AI-assisted, both unverified
what: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and Claude found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Hours earlier, he and NYU's Tristan Buckmaster posted an AI-assisted proof that the Navier–Stokes fluid equations can blow up with no outside force.
why: This is the verification bottleneck in its purest form: AI can now produce more 'proof' than humans can check. Any AI feature with high-stakes output needs a checking layer you trust, not just a better generator.

tryThis.text: Next time an AI output 'passes the tests', ask what the tests actually check. Here, a Lean proof compiling doesn't show the theorem it proves is the famous one.

real.label: Huge if true · unverified
real.reason: Credible authors and formal proofs exist, but the Riemann claim has no readable paper, the Navier–Stokes proof's numerical certificate isn't released, and no outside expert has confirmed either.

headline: Nasdaq's worst week since March 2020 as the AI trade cracks
what: The Nasdaq fell 10% this week, and the S&P 500 and Dow closed Friday in correction. Anthropic's record IPO rose 17% on day one, then gave most of that back by Friday.
why: When capital gets expensive, AI spend gets judged on ROI. Expect harder questions on revenue per AI feature, more pressure to run cheaper models in production, and fewer 'AI everywhere' roadmaps.

headline: Gemini can now drive your Mac's apps for you, in a background window
what: Google rolled out 'computer use' in the Gemini Mac app on 19 November. It clicks, types and fills in forms across local files, desktop apps and websites in an isolated window, so your own screen stays free.
why: Agents are moving from APIs to the UI. If your product has no API, agents will use your screens anyway, so clear labels, stable layouts and explicit confirm steps now serve robots as well as people.

tryThis.text: Write one weekly 10-click chore as a single-paragraph instruction. If you can't describe it clearly, an agent can't do it either. (Gemini's version is US-only for now.)

real.label: Shipped · US paid plans
real.reason: Live according to Google's own post, but limited to US English, paid AI Plus/Pro/Ultra plans and Apple Silicon Macs.
